decision_reason: Iteration 1 surfaced strong leads — particularly the FDA/CDC cucumber outbreak (June 2024, 449 cases, 31 states) and the Milo's Poultry Farms eggs outbreak (illnesses starting May 23, 2024) — but several critical gaps remain. First, the CDC cucumber outbreak index page (africana-06-24) returned only a brief snippet without full case/death/hospitalization counts; the full investigation update with final figures needs to be targeted. Second, the eggs outbreak page covers illnesses starting May 23, 2024, squarely within the target window, but the snippet only shows September/October 2024 update counts — an earlier update covering May–July 2024 specifically is needed. Third, the backyard poultry outbreak (513 sick, 134 hospitalized, 1 death) surfaced via an X/CDC tweet but lacks a date anchor — this may be a 2024 or 2025 event and needs a direct CDC investigation page. Fourth, the FSIS.usda.gov results (2 domains) were not summarized — USDA/FSIS may have issued recall/outbreak notices for poultry or meat-linked Salmonella in the target window. Fifth, no state-level subnational data (beyond state counts) has been confirmed, and the doh.wa.gov result was not summarized. Iteration 2 must close these gaps within the 4-query limit before the max-2-iteration bound is reached.
coverage_assessment: Partial. Two confirmed outbreak events within the target window have been identified (cucumbers June 2024; eggs starting May 23 2024). However, full quantitative fields (confirmed cases, hospitalizations, deaths, subnational breakdown) are not yet confirmed from page text — only snippets. The backyard poultry outbreak date is unconfirmed for the target window. FSIS and state-level sources are unsummarized. No MMWR or FoodNet annual summary has been identified yet for 2024 Salmonella totals.

Social media (Facebook 4, X 2) low trust. CIDRAP (2) is a reputable secondary source. Wikipedia, allrecipes.com, beaconbio.org are low-value. Need: direct CDC investigation page for backyard poultry 2024, FSIS meat/poultry Salmonella recall data, and state-level subnational detail.
trustworthiness_assessment: CDC and FDA results are highest trust. CIDRAP is reputable secondary. Facebook/X posts are low trust and should only corroborate, not anchor data. Wikipedia and allrecipes.com are not usable as evidence sources. The doh.wa.gov result is potentially high-trust for subnational data but was not summarized.
disease_location_time_fit_assessment: Disease fit: strong (Salmonella confirmed across all results). Location fit: strong (US multistate). Time fit: partially confirmed — cucumber outbreak active June–July 2024 fits; eggs outbreak starts May 23 2024 fits; backyard poultry outbreak date unconfirmed (the X tweet has no date anchor and the CDC URL slug does not indicate 2024); May 2025 and July 2025 CDC pages are out of scope and should be excluded.
corroboration_potential_assessment: The cucumber outbreak has both an FDA page and a CDC page — good corroboration potential. The eggs outbreak has a CDC page. The backyard poultry outbreak needs a CDC investigation page to corroborate the X tweet. FSIS results could corroborate USDA-regulated product recalls. A targeted CDC backyard poultry 2024 query and an FSIS/USDA Salmonella 2024 query are the highest-priority follow-ups.
